- Overestimate prices when sentiment is high (especially >0.7) — reduce forecast by 2–5% for high sentiment days.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low (especially <0.3) — add 3–7% to forecast for low sentiment days.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes — apply a 1–3 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 1–2% per day post-spike.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–3% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid overconfidence in early forecast days — reduce first 5 days by 1–3% if sentiment is weak or volatile.
- If sentiment drops sharply after forecast, adjust downward by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days to reflect risk-off behavior.
